segments: Qatar-based freight forwarders managing cross-border GCC and transshipment cargo via Hamad Port — primary adopters of customs doc automation
Mid-market 3PLs in Qatar and the GCC offering e-commerce fulfillment, last-mile dispatch, and contract logistics to retail and FMCG brands
Energy-sector logistics operators (oil, gas, petrochemicals) requiring HS code compliance, bonded cargo, and hazmat documentation workflows
GCC customs brokers and clearing agents handling high volumes of HS code classification, duty calculations, and single-window filings
Regional logistics arms of multinational manufacturers managing multi-country GCC distribution with fragmented ERP and TMS stacks
pain_points: Manual customs documentation — spreadsheets and email chains across customs brokers, forwarders, and port authorities — causes delays and errors, especially as the GCC Integrated Customs Tariff added 5,600 new HS codes effective January 2025
No standardized geocoding in many GCC residential and commercial zones makes last-mile dispatch coordination error-prone, requiring manual address resolution and driver re-routing

Fragmented handoff between freight forwarders (customs clearance) and 3PLs (last-mile) creates coordination gaps: receiving schedules, container unloading times, and inventory transfers are managed across separate systems with no unified data layer
Legacy ERP and TMS platforms lack real-time customs status visibility, forcing operations teams to chase clearance updates manually rather than triggering dispatch workflows automatically
Varying customs procedures and compliance rules across the six GCC member states force forwarders to maintain separate filing workflows per country, adding cost and extending lead times
key_players: GWC (Gulf Warehousing Company): Qatar's largest logistics provider with freight forwarding, customs clearance, last-mile delivery, and e-commerce fulfillment — actively investing in AI-driven route optimization and digital fleet management

Milaha (Qatar Navigation Q.P.S.C.): Qatar's dominant maritime and logistics conglomerate offering integrated freight forwarding, customs clearance, port management, and supply chain solutions; signed Oracle and Google Cloud MoUs to accelerate digital transformation

Aramex: GCC-wide freight forwarding and last-mile operator undergoing 'Accelerate28' transformation, recently restructured into separate Express and Logistics B2B divisions with dedicated GCC commercial and operations teams

Kuehne+Nagel (GCC+ Cluster): Global forwarder with active Qatar operations, newly appointed MD Leon Diradourian effective June 2025, and a customs development background; operates e-commerce fulfillment hub in Dubai targeting GCC-wide customers

CargoWise (WiseTech Global): Enterprise SaaS incumbent for customs clearance and freight management in 190+ countries — the primary global platform legacy forwarders are locked into, making GCC-native, lighter-weight alternatives a credible wedge

call_targets.name: Matthew Kearns
call_targets.rationale: Recently confirmed Group CEO after serving as Acting CEO; GWC is Qatar's largest 3PL and freight forwarder, publicly investing in AI-powered dispatch, last-mile automation, and customs documentation workflows. Kearns has spoken directly about building an 'integrated logistics platform' — exactly the layer this SaaS product targets.

call_targets.name: Sheikh Abdulla Bin Fahad Bin Jassim Al Thani
call_targets.rationale: As Group MD, he sets GWC's portfolio diversification and trade facilitation strategy, including expansion into free zones and cross-border corridors. His mandate to support Qatar NVision 2030 supply chain goals makes him a key decision-maker for any platform touching customs clearance and dispatch coordination.

call_targets.name: Leon Diradourian
call_targets.rationale: Appointed June 2025 to lead all GCC operations including Qatar; his most recent role was VP of Strategic Customs Development overseeing the Farrow customs brokerage integration — making him one of the most contextually relevant executives to discuss customs documentation automation and its fit for mid-market GCC forwarders.

call_targets.name: Mohammad Alkhas
call_targets.role: Chief Operating Officer — Freight and Logistics
call_targets.rationale: Leads Aramex's entire B2B freight forwarding and logistics operations across the GCC under the Accelerate28 transformation program; Aramex recently restructured its freight and last-mile units into separate P&Ls, making this an active moment to discuss operational tooling gaps in customs doc automation and last-mile dispatch.

call_targets.name: Fadi Azzi
call_targets.rationale: Publicly named as lead on Aramex's new healthcare logistics hub in Dubai South, handling integrated freight forwarding, customs clearance, and last-mile distribution for pharmaceutical and regulated goods — a high-complexity segment where documentation automation ROI is immediate and measurable.

outreach.subject: Customs automation for your GCC+ footprint — quick question
outreach.body: Leon — your background leading the Farrow customs brokerage integration at K+N before moving to the GCC makes you one of the few people who's seen both the technology and the operational side of customs documentation at scale. We're building a B2B SaaS platform that automates customs declaration workflows and last-mile dispatch coordination specifically for freight forwarders and 3PLs in the GCC, and Qatar is our launch market. Given you're now overseeing Qatar, Saudi, UAE, and six other countries from Dubai, I'd love 20 minutes to understand where the documentation and handoff pain sits hardest in your cluster. Would a call next week work?
